summary: Independently reconstructed the repository-wide mutation inventory rather than trusting Phase 149A's summary as ground truth: found 13 real, CLI-reachable mutation dispatch sites across src/pcae/commands/push.py, src/pcae/core/agent.py, src/pcae/commands/task.py, and src/pcae/commands/phase.py (up from 149A's >=8 framing) -- 2 Permission-Broker-gated (both pcae push sites, PBPC-001 v1.2), 11 not. Two genuinely new findings beyond 149A's inventory: (1) pcae promote (core/agent.py's ECP/EPR/PER promotion-execution pipeline, build_promotion_execution) is a real production file-write/delete mechanism whose own docstring calls it 'the only PCAE code path that mutates root', gated only on a self-declared --promotion-authorized boolean flag, and not excluded from targeting src/pcae/** itself; (2) commands/task.py's two git-commit sites (pcae task finish --commit, pcae task finish recover --message) were not previously inventoried. Defined an 8-category mutation taxonomy (M1 working-tree mutation through M8 external-system mutation) using repository-native ACTION_*/EXECUTION_CLASS_* vocabulary from permission_broker_foundation.py where it already exists. Built current Permission-Broker coverage matrix (only pcae push covered), Runtime-Enforcement coverage matrix (RE remains an unconnected parallel track per PBPC-001 Section 25, wired to none of the 13 sites), and authority/approval matrix (confirmation vs approval vs permission kept structurally distinct; found that the only path with named approval-evidence fields, final-verification-tooling-push-decision's --approve-keep/--approved-by/--reason, is still unauthenticated). Found PBPA-001's existing vocabulary (ACTION_COMMIT, ACTION_ROLLBACK, EXECUTION_CLASS_ROLLBACK, POL-004's existing mutation-vs-rollback approval-requirement distinction) already anticipates most of this chapter's needs -- no new request schema required to begin. Evaluated five candidate architecture models (A: per-command PB integration: rejected, duplication already occurring organically -- three independently-built adoption pipelines share no code; B: shared adapter alone: rejected, does not stop below-adapter bypass; C: centralized universal executor: rejected, would require rewriting genuinely distinct existing structural-validation logic beyond architecture-only scope; D: Runtime Enforcement as the mutation boundary: rejected, explicitly out of scope per PBPC-001 Section 25; E: Hybrid -- canonical request reusing PermissionBrokerRequest, unchanged -> Permission Broker decision, unchanged POL-001..012 -> thin per-mutation-class adapter modeled on push.py's proven pattern -> existing dispatch/mechanical validation, unchanged). SELECTED: Model E. Recorded legacy-path dispositions (pcae remote */pcae promote: BROKER_WIRE; backend-created-output-adoption push and final-verification-tooling-push: ROUTE_TO_CANONICAL_COMMAND; pcae task finish paths: KEEP_SEPARATE/LIFECYCLE_INTERNAL), a full threat model (direct bypass, agent self-permission, legacy alternate path, stale ALLOW, policy downgrading, approval fabrication, partial mutation, rollback abuse, mechanical override), and Chapter 149 scope (IN: commit/push/rollback/file-apply across agent.py/task.py/phase.py; OUT: lifecycle bookkeeping under .pcae/**, canonical artifact publication M7, external notifications M8, manual human git, tests, Prompt Creation/Dispatch/agent invocation/runtime activation). This phase is architecture/inventory-only: no production code, contract, or POL-001..012 meaning was changed; no new Permission Broker production consumer was added; no mutation path was modified, activated, or exercised -- every finding is pre-existing code, independently observed only. Production diff: git diff --name-only 55a1f8aa..HEAD -- src/pcae/ empty. Contract diff: git diff --name-only 55a1f8aa..HEAD -- docs/contracts/ empty (PBPC-001 remains v1.2, PBPA-001 remains v1.0). Runtime reconfirmed Observed/observe/unavailable before and after. See docs/PHASE_149B_REPOSITORY_WIDE_MUTATION_PERMISSION_COVERAGE_ARCHITECTURE.md for full detail.
tests_added_or_updated: No new test files (architecture/inventory-only phase; no production code changed, so no new tests were required). Validation ran via CLI governance commands only: pcae health, pcae check, pcae status coherence, pcae doctor task-memory, pcae push check, pcae runtime inspect, pcae notify status, pcae phase-report show --latest, pcae phase-report reconcile --phase-id 149A -- all ran clean at phase start and were re-run clean before completion.

validation_results.name: mutation_taxonomy
validation_results.result: Defined an 8-category mutation taxonomy (M1 working-tree mutation through M8 external-system mutation), anchored to repository-native ACTION_*/EXECUTION_CLASS_* constants in permission_broker_foundation.py where they already exist (ACTION_SOURCE_MUTATION, ACTION_COMMIT, ACTION_PUSH, ACTION_ROLLBACK, EXECUTION_CLASS_ROLLBACK).

validation_results.name: permission_broker_and_runtime_enforcement_coverage_matrices
validation_results.result: Built current PB coverage matrix (2 of 13 sites covered, both pcae push, PBPC-001 v1.2) and RE coverage matrix (0 of 13 sites; RE remains an unconnected parallel track per PBPC-001 Section 25 PBPC-REQ-085/086, confirmed via direct inspection of backend_invocations.py and runtime_enforcement_safety_authorization.py -- every readiness/authorization function returns design-only/non-executing).

validation_results.name: authority_approval_matrix_and_pol004_finding
validation_results.result: Built an authority/approval matrix preserving confirmation vs approval vs permission distinctions per instruction; found POL-004 (Missing Human Approval) in permission_broker_foundation.py already scopes to EXECUTION_CLASS_SHELL/BACKEND/ADAPTER/ROLLBACK and explicitly excludes EXECUTION_CLASS_MUTATION/NONE (PBPA-REQ-063/064) -- i.e. existing policy semantics already distinguish push/commit (no approval required) from rollback (approval required), a load-bearing finding for the architecture decision.

validation_results.name: architecture_model_evaluation_and_selection
validation_results.result: Evaluated Models A-E per instruction; selected Model E (Hybrid: canonical PermissionBrokerRequest, unchanged -> Permission Broker decision, unchanged POL-001..012 -> thin per-mutation-class adapter modeled on push.py's proven freshness-then-dispatch pattern -> existing structural-validation/dispatch, unchanged). Rejected A (duplication already occurring: pcae remote *, pcae promote, and backend-created-output-adoption are three independently-built adoption pipelines sharing no code), B (does not by itself stop below-adapter direct dispatch), C (would require rewriting distinct existing mechanical-validation logic in commit_file_changes/execute_rollback/build_promotion_execution), and D (explicitly out of scope per PBPC-001 Section 25; wrong domain -- RE governs shell/backend/adapter invocation, not direct git/file mutation).

validation_results.name: threat_model_and_legacy_disposition
validation_results.result: Recorded a 9-item threat model (direct bypass, agent self-permission, legacy alternate path, stale ALLOW, policy downgrading, approval fabrication, partial mutation, rollback abuse, mechanical override) and explicit per-path legacy dispositions (BROKER_WIRE / ROUTE_TO_CANONICAL_COMMAND / KEEP_SEPARATE) for every one of the 13 inventoried sites, per instruction not to leave any path's disposition ambiguous.

validation_results.name: chapter_149_scope_definition
